articles.title: 토큰화된 펀드의 유동성 착시: 24시간 거래와 실물 자산 상환 사이의 간극을 해소하다
articles.excerpt: 블록체인 기술의 등장은 수많은 산업에 깊은 변화를 가져왔으며, 그중 금융 분야는 혁명의 선두에 서 있다. 탈중앙화 금융(DeFi)과 분산원장기술(DLT)이 제시하는 가장 매력적인 약속 중 하나는 광범위한 자산에 대한 유동성, 투명성, 접근성을 높이는 잠재력이다. 실물 자산(RWA)이나 전통 금융 상품에 대한 부분 소유권을 블록체인상에 나타내는 토큰화된 펀드…
articles.body: 블록체인 기술의 등장은 수많은 산업에 깊은 변화를 가져왔으며, 그중 금융 분야는 혁명의 선두에 서 있다. 탈중앙화 금융(DeFi)과 분산원장기술(DLT)이 제시하는 가장 매력적인 약속 중 하나는 광범위한 자산에 대한 유동성, 투명성, 접근성을 높이는 잠재력이다. 실물 자산(RWA)이나 전통 금융 상품에 대한 부분 소유권을 블록체인상에 나타내는 토큰화된 펀드는 이러한 약속의 정수라 할 수 있다. 이들은 24시간 거래, 즉각적인 결제, 그리고 운영 오버헤드 감소의 매력을 제공하며, 기존 금융 시장의 한계를 뛰어넘는 듯 보인다. 그러나 이러한 끊임없는 거래의 빛나는 표면 아래에는 종종 오해되는 중요한 역학, 즉 "유동성 착시"가 숨어 있다. 이 착시는 블록체인 2차 시장에서 토큰이 즉각적이고 24시간 내내 거래될 수 있다는 점과, 그 기반이 되는 실물 자산을 법정화폐나 다른 유동성 있는 수단으로 상환하는 본질적으로 느리고 종종 제약받는 과정 사이에 존재하는 근본적인 단절에서 비롯된다. 부동산 포트폴리오나 미국 국채 펀드의 지분을 나타내는 토큰은 탈중앙화 거래소(DEX)나 중앙화된 디지털 자산 플랫폼에서 언제든지 거래될 수 있지만, 그 토큰을 기초 자산의 가치로 실제로 전환하는 과정, 즉 1차 시장 상환은 여전히 오프체인 자산의 운영 현실, 규제 프레임워크, 그리고 내재된 유동성 특성에 묶여 있다. 이 글은 이러한 중요한 간극을 깊이 파고들어 그 메커니즘을 분석하고, 실제 사례를 검토하며, 토큰화된 펀드의 진정한 보편적 유동성 실현을 가로막는 한계를 탐구한다.

articles.title: The Liquidity Illusion in Tokenized Funds: Bridging the Chasm Between 24/7 Trading and Real-World Redemption
articles.excerpt: Introduction The advent of blockchain technology has sparked a profound transformation across numerous industries, with finance standing at the forefront of this revolution. One of the most compelling…
articles.body: Introduction The advent of blockchain technology has sparked a profound transformation across numerous industries, with finance standing at the forefront of this revolution. One of the most compelling promises of decentralized finance (DeFi) and distributed ledger technology (DLT) lies in its potential to enhance liquidity, transparency, and accessibility for a wide array of assets. Tokenized funds, which represent fractional ownership in real-world assets (RWAs) or traditional financial instruments on a blockchain, epitomize this promise. They offer the allure of 24/7 trading, atomic settlement, and reduced operational overhead, seemingly transcending the limitations of conventional financial markets.

articles.body: This article was created with the help of AI. The test, the posts and the numbers come from my own news pipeline. On October 8 I ran ten of my news posts through two Claude models. Opus 5.5 already wrote them for me every day. Fable 5.1 is the bigger model, and its price per token is 2.5 times higher. A blind reviewer preferred Opus in six of the ten posts, each time by a slight margin. Fable took twice as long and cost 3.2 times as much per post. I run two AI news feeds, Claude News and Promtime. Claude takes an English source and rewrites it into a post by each channel's rules. Claude News is for developers: Claude releases, the API, pricing. Promtime covers AI in general, in plainer language.

articles.title: I Built a Flutter Plugin That Generates Crypto Keys Inside Your Phone's Hardware Chip
articles.excerpt: Flutter has no native way to generate a cryptographic key inside the device's hardware security chip and sign something with it. You can store keys in the Secure Enclave on iOS or StrongBox on Android…
articles.body: Flutter has no native way to generate a cryptographic key inside the device's hardware security chip and sign something with it. You can store keys in the Secure Enclave on iOS or StrongBox on Android, but you have to write Swift and Kotlin yourself, bridge it through method channels, handle the three different signature formats each platform returns, and then figure out how to make the result usable for Ethereum's account abstraction standards. I spent 8 weeks doing exactly that, and the result is chainkey . The actual problem I was building a Web3 authentication flow in Flutter. The requirement: seedless wallets. No mnemonic phrase, no "write down these 12 words." The private key lives in the Secure Enclave (iOS) or StrongBox (Android) and never leaves the chip.

articles.body: The FDE Mindset Shift: From Code Craftsmanship to Organizational Rewiring TLDR: The strongest senior engineers often have the hardest first quarter as Forward Deployed Engineers. The role is not mostly writing code — it's integration archaeology and organizational negotiation with some code attached. The ones who thrive stop optimizing the artifact and start optimizing the adoption. The Ticket Is a Lie Here's the pattern that keeps repeating, and if you've made this transition yourself, you felt it in roughly week two. A senior backend engineer — the kind who's genuinely good, the kind teams fight to keep — takes an FDE rotation. They arrive at the host tribe with a strong instinct for craft: understand the domain, design the thing properly, build it clean. They ask for tickets.

articles.title: NASA astronaut Jessica Watkins is the 1st Black woman to command a space mission. Will we see more diversity in the future on the final frontier?
articles.excerpt: "Diversity makes the crew stronger."
articles.body: When Jessica Watkins became commander of her mission to the International Space Station, she didn't just fulfill her duty as an astronaut — she made history. Watkins is commanding SpaceX's Crew-13 mission , which launched her and three other astronauts to the I nternational Space Station on Oct. 1. As their Crew Dragon capsule lifted off atop a Falcon 9 rocket that day, Watkins became the first Black woman to command a crewed mission to space. Spaceflight and space science are historically white and male-dominated fields, so this milestone carries incredible significance. "This is certainly an important milestone, I think both for our agency and for the country," Watkins said in a press briefing ahead of Crew-13's launch. This is Watkins' second spaceflight.

articles.title: The M6 MacBook Pro is probably the last of its kind
articles.excerpt: Pictured: A great screen, best-in-class laptop, fine keyboard, and a very comfortable blanket (sold separately). | Photo: Nathan Edwards / The Verge On November 6th, Apple will release an all-new MacB…
articles.body: Pictured: A great screen, best-in-class laptop, fine keyboard, and a very comfortable blanket (sold separately). | Photo: Nathan Edwards / The Verge On November 6th, Apple will release an all-new MacBook Pro. It's thinner and lighter and has a beautiful OLED touchscreen. It is very likely what every new MacBook Pro will look like in a couple of years. The M6 MacBook Pro, which is also out on the 6th, is not that laptop. Instead, it's a straightforward chip bump of Apple's entry-level MacBook Pro, in basically the same chassis Apple's been using since 2021 . Everything that was great about the M5 MacBook Pro last year, and the M4 the year before , still applies. The M6 MacBook Pro is still a great all-around computer, and a nice step up from the MacBook Air.
articles.author: Nathan Edwards

articles.title: The touchscreen MacBook Pro is a winner
articles.excerpt: You can look, and you can touch. (Note: all the photos in this review are of the 16-inch PROLED Pro.) | Photo: Owen Grove / The Verge I keep forgetting the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display has a to…
articles.body: You can look, and you can touch. (Note: all the photos in this review are of the 16-inch PROLED Pro.) | Photo: Owen Grove / The Verge I keep forgetting the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display has a touchscreen. I've been testing this new laptop, one of the most impressive Apple has ever created, for the better part of a week. I can't stop noticing some of its other features: the slimmer design, the improved display, the Dynamic Island that somehow catches my eye more than the notch ever did. But I keep forgetting that as I go about my day, I can now reach out and poke the screen. Come to think of it, that might be exactly what Apple intended. Steve Jobs said touch laptops were a bad idea; some subset of users demanded one anyway. Now the MacBook Pro has one.

articles.title: NASA announces experimental X-70 Fractal aircraft: A 'new beginning for aeronautics'
articles.excerpt: NASA has announced its next X-plane, known as the X-70 Fractal, designed to test advanced maneuverability and which will feature a rapidly reconfigurable design.
articles.body: NASA has revealed a glimpse of its next X-plane, known as the X-70 Fractal. Or at least what it thinks the X-70 will look like once built. The agency released a short statement on Wednesday (Nov. 4) announcing the X-plane , or experimental plane, declaring it to be a highly maneuverable test bed with a "rapidly reconfigurable flight-control technology," allowing NASA to swap both external and internal components on-the-fly. This modular architecture will allow NASA to "explore aircraft maneuverability in ways never before demonstrated in crewed flight," according to the agency's statement . The announcement was made alongside an AI-generated image showing two canted vertical tail fins emerging from swirling smoke.

articles.title: China lays out plans to land astronauts on the moon 'before 2030.' Can NASA still win this race?
articles.excerpt: China has laid out its roadmap for landing astronauts on the moon "before 2030," a milestone that NASA hopes to achieve in 2028.
articles.body: China has given us some details about the epic moon landing it plans to pull off a few years from now. Chinese officials laid out the roadmap for its crewed lunar campaign at the 7th Manned Space Symposium, which was held Oct. 31 and Nov. 1 in Beijing. The campaign consists of four missions, culminating in a crewed touchdown "before 2030," according to media reports . That timeline — which is consistent with previous statements made by the China Manned Space Agency — keeps the pressure on the U.S., which aims to put its own astronauts down on the moon in 2028, via NASA's Artemis program .
